name: 2127-2129 Prairie Avenue — the double building of flats, K01 frontage assembly
aka: 2129 S. Prairie Avenue (the second half of the double building)

function.note: The 1911 sheet letters each half of the building 'F', its key's flat, and prints '3B' in each: two three-storey buildings of flats on a basement under one front, divided by a party wall, numbered 2127 (north) and 2129 (south). The T-1842 census rules the building present in 1904 (present_as_mapped) and the register's family row reads it as brick masonry; that it held flats in 1904, as in 1911, is inferred from the plan the sheet draws (two halves, each with its own entrance), not from a 1904 record.

research_note: T-1931 (the S19 package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id: the building is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits (K03 brick walls, K06 sash, K07's paired-leaf entrance in a round-arched opening on a broad stone stoop, K09 stone lintels, K10 bracketed cornice under a flat roof, K01's rear veranda in three decks) instead of the draft builder. What is read: sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size: '3B' and 'F' in each half; a brick main body 24.0 m deep and 13.85 m along the front, built to the south lot line; a party wall from front to rear 6.74 m from the north wall, its thickness figure printed on it; two small stoops at the front, one either side of the party wall; shallow light-court recesses in both flanks; the key's composition-or-gravel roof dot in each half; and a three-storey open frame porch (dashed, '3') across the party wall at the rear. No photograph, plate or description of the building is known (the Prairie library holds none under 2127 or 2129; its 1890s view down the east side of the block, a20-glessner-2100-block-east-side-1890s, shows a flat-topped block at its far edge behind the trees that no reading identifies, and a building in the corner of a street view does not attest it). So every height, opening, material and detail is the kits' reconstruction under liberty L-k01-2127-prairie-1931. The lot to the south, 2141, is a non-building frontage and stays open ground. Review: docs/RESEARCH/k01-2127-flats-1931/README.md.

documented_range.note: The building claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws it and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are not read.

position.symbolic_location: 2127 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2127 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body on its north side (lot frame u 23.5, v -6.1 m from the middle of the rear lot line), read off the 1911 sheet 35 raster at full size (T-1931) through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, which carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading. The draft's fit stood its corner 0.6 m south of the north wall, short of it because the light courts bite into the flank; the corner moves to the wall. Rotation turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body, the three-storey brick block the sheet draws: 24.0 m from the rear wall (column 1049) to the front wall (column 916) and 13.85 m along the front, from the north wall (row 1458) to the south wall on the lot line (row 1533), read at full size off the raster and checked against the committed trace (s35fp-2127-b1 p1). The light-court recesses in both flanks (about 0.6-0.9 m deep, 9.5-14.5 m and 18.4-20.6 m back from the front) are not cut into it: K01 lays the main body as one rectangle.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet in each half: three full storeys on a basement.

construction.note: The sheet colours the building pink, its key's brick building, with no stone-front edge along the front line.

chimneys.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two plain brick stacks rising through the roof on the party wall, serving both flats' ranges; the sheet draws no chimney (L-k01-2127-prairie-1931).

entrance_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the sheet draws two stoops side by side, one either side of the party wall, so each flat has its own door at the building's middle. K01 builds one entrance, so the two doors are the K07 kit's pair of leaves, one a flat, in one round-headed opening 2.0 m wide on the party wall's line, cut in the brick under the principal storey's arch band (street_front_round_heads). front_yard_m is the street grid's own distance: the front stands about 7.15 m behind the Prairie Avenue street line and the walk begins 1 ft further out (L-k01-2127-prairie-1931).

rear_veranda.note: RECONSTRUCTED in its parts, its place READ: the sheet draws an open frame porch (yellow, dashed outline, '3') against the rear wall across the party wall, columns 1046-1071 and rows 1478-1513: out 4.55 m from the rear wall and along it from 3.54 to 10.06 m from the north corner (the committed trace's part p2 agrees within 0.1 m). Built as K01's rear veranda three decks high, one deck at each flat floor (1.5, 5.3 and 8.8 m), on paired timber posts at four stations, railed, with a flight down to the yard off the lower deck; the decks' heights are the storeys', its posts, rails and the flight's place the module's. The flights between the decks are not built. The draft stood it as a closed two-storey frame range (L-k01-2127-prairie-1931).

boundary.note: RECONSTRUCTED: no boundary across the front; no picture of it is held and the district draft stood none. The lot's sides are parcel prairie_2127's (data/street_grid/1904.json) in this frame, measured from the south corner (L-k01-2127-prairie-1931).

yard.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K14 kit's walk of flags from the stoop's foot straight out to the public walk, 2.0 m wide for the two flats' traffic (L-k01-2127-prairie-1931).
